You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Dobro Dobro is a fast and fun climbing game where you have 3 options on your turn: play a card higher than the value in play, play two identical cards and double their value, or play a card with the same value in play to double it! If you can't play any card... That's bad! Put all cards in play in your score pile and start a new climbing. When a player plays the last card in their hand, the round ends and players receive points based on the cards in the score pile. The less cards you have, the more points you get! So, take advantage of the special cards, using them at the right time in order to change the direction of play, skip your turn or even play any number to avoid getting cards. You can play a special card You can take all played cards and add them to your score pile At end of turn, draw back to 6. Round End After the draw pile is emptied, the next player to empty their hand ends the round Any hand and play cards are discarded Gain points depending on how many score cards you have compared to other players (more cards = less points) Game End The game ends after 3 rounds, the player with the most points wins! [Rating: 1/10] The kind of game you play while having a casual conversation or over drinks. As such, it's very simple, random and there isn't much to it.

[Rating: 1/10] Wait, this is literally just Knizia's Escalation, with a few minor differences changing 2% of it. Even the card distribution for almost all of the values are exactly the same! But the rules are messier and more confusing, for such a light game. You can only play doubles, instead of however many you want? Huh?  I do like Escalation, so I wouldn't mind this but.... plagiarizing it is kinda gross.

[Rating: 2/10] Played once. Hated. Forced to play again, still managed to hate it even more.  Just not my type of game

[Rating: 2/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  Kind of a bit of Uno with some additional rules that double the power of the cards when you match, etc. We played one round and decided we had enough.

[Rating: 3/10] Ladder climbing game that manages to feel worse to play than most despite being pretty similar to Uno and other games with its distribution of cards. Luck just plays way too high of a factor in the game, frequently leaving you a single play on your turn if any. My big issue stems from the special cards, though. The end of each round seems to come down to a game of hot potato with everyone trying to avoid taking the insurmountable pile of cards in the middle and the only recourse you have against that is randomly having drawn a special card previously. [Rating: 3/10] Least favorite of the card shedding games I've played recently. It's fun if you have the cards you need, it's not if you don't.

[Rating: 3/10] There's just so many better climbing games out there than this one there's no reason to get into arguments over how to interpret the rules over matching cards and how it all works...and it doesn't really do anything to set itself apart.
